title: strange behaviour with remapped Win+C → Win+V

status.label: Verify Win+C to Win+V release ordering
status.detail: A maintainer reproduced the clipboard-history window closing when Win is released after a Win+C-to-Win+V remap on Windows 11.

judgment.rationale: The issue gives a specific Win+C-to-Win+V mapping and reports that clipboard history opens but closes when Win is released. The reporter says native Win+V remains open after releasing Win, and a maintainer reproduced the remapped case on Windows 11, identifying the release order as a relevant discriminator. Open issue #14556 is a different failure where remapped Ctrl changes the paste shortcut emitted by clipboard history; it does not cover this popup-dismissal behavior.
evidence: The report lists PowerToys 0.59.1 on Windows 11 and maps Win+C to Win+V.
The clipboard-history surface opens, then closes after Win is released.
The reporter says native Win+V remains open after releasing Win.
A maintainer reproduced the issue on Windows 11 and noted the C-up then Win-up sequence.
Open issue #14556 concerns Ctrl remapping causing clipboard history selection to type v instead of pasting; it is a separate symptom.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce on current Windows and PowerToys, trace the injected Win/V key-down and key-up order, and prevent a remapped shortcut from dismissing the destination surface on modifier release.

fix_assessment.rationale: The maintainer reproduction isolates key-up ordering for the remapped Win+V activation. If the injected destination chord is released in a way that dismisses the clipboard surface, preserve the destination activation's expected release semantics.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve the clipboard-history surface after a remapped Win+V
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The remapping path may release the Windows modifier before the injected V key-up or otherwise expose a release sequence that causes the clipboard-history surface to dismiss.
plan: Reproduce Win+C-to-Win+V on current Windows and compare its injected key-down/up order with native Win+V.
Trace source C and Win release handling through the shortcut remap path to identify which event dismisses the surface.
If the remap emits an invalid or premature release sequence, adjust the injected key-up ordering while preserving source-key cleanup.
Add regression coverage for both source-key-first and modifier-first release orders.
verification: The Win+C-to-Win+V remap opens clipboard history and it remains open after all source keys are released.
Native Win+V continues to work and other Win-key remaps release cleanly.
No modifier remains logically pressed after either release order.

confidence.rationale: A maintainer reproduced the issue and the release-order sequence is documented, but current event tracing is needed to distinguish injected key-up ordering from Windows clipboard-surface behavior.

issue_context.summary: A Win+C-to-Win+V remap opens clipboard history but reportedly closes it when the Windows modifier is released.
known_information: The report lists PowerToys 0.59.1 on Windows 11.
The reporter maps Win+C to Win+V and says the clipboard-history surface closes on Win release.
The reporter says native Win+V remains open after Win release.
A maintainer reproduced the remapped behavior and highlighted the source-key/modifier release order.
Open issue #14556 covers a separate Ctrl-remapping interaction that changes the paste action after selecting clipboard history.
inferences: The injected Win/V release sequence may differ from the native shortcut and dismiss the clipboard-history surface.
issue_context.analysis: The issue is distinct from #14556: this report concerns the destination popup closing, not the selected clipboard item being typed as a character. A focused key-event comparison should identify whether Keyboard Manager emits a premature release.
initial_investigation: Read the issue body and all three comments, including the reporter's distinction from native Win+V and the maintainer's release-order reproduction.
Reviewed open issue #14556; its Ctrl-remapping/paste symptom does not cover popup dismissal after Win+C-to-Win+V.

information_gaps.information: Whether the popup-dismissal behavior persists on current PowerToys and Windows, and which of the source-key-first or modifier-first release orders triggers it
information_gaps.why_needed: The report and maintainer reproduction are from 2022 and the issue does not establish current event order or OS behavior.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Repeat the Win+C-to-Win+V mapping on current stable and compare releasing C before Win with releasing Win before C.

actions.label: Confirm the current clipboard popup behavior

comment.body: A maintainer reproduced the clipboard-history popup closing after a Win+C-to-Win+V remap on Windows 11. Could you confirm whether this still happens on current PowerToys and Windows, and whether it depends on releasing C before Win or Win before C?

actions.label: Reproduce clipboard history dismissal by release order

reproduce.title: Compare release orders for Win+C-to-Win+V
steps: Press Win+C and confirm clipboard history opens.
Release C while keeping Win pressed, then release Win; observe whether the popup closes.
Repeat while releasing Win before C.
Compare with native Win+V using both release orders.
reproduce.expected_result: The clipboard-history surface remains open after the remapped shortcut is fully released, matching the native Win+V behavior.
